prompt: You are a captain choosing teams in PE. Your best friend expects to be picked first, as usual, but another classmate is chosen last almost every week and is already looking at the floor. What is the fairest approach?

options.text: Pick your best friend first as promised, because loyalty matters more than one PE lesson
Pick the strongest players first every time, so your team wins and nobody can complain
Deliberately pick your friend last once, so they learn how the overlooked player feels
Pick to build a balanced team, give the player who is usually chosen last an early pick, and tell your friend honestly beforehand that you are picking for fairness, not favourites

explanation: Choosing a balanced side and explaining your reasoning to your friend respects both the game and the player who is usually overlooked. Always picking your friend first teaches everyone else that the teams are fixed before anyone plays.
